fair_value_reason: FY28 EPS $25.0 (FY27 $22.7 x 1.10) x ~38x forward = $950, less ~$12 of expected special-dividend drag (~62% x ~$20) = ~$938. I trim to ~$935 for a 10-yr yield at 5.24% and rising, which argues against the 38.5x-40x hold cases. Shares 443.3M; net cash is not added separately, because the P/E already capitalizes its interest income. This is close to the round-2 mean ($933) and ~1.5% above $921.20.
supervisor_summary: The round-2 forecasts converge on FY28 EPS $25 x ~38x forward, less a special-dividend drag, for a fair value of ~$933. The narrower range comes from shared inputs, not new independent evidence. The special-dividend deduction is right for an unadjusted price target. History (five specials with 26-43 month gaps, the last in Dec 2023) supports ~60-65% odds and a ~$12 drag, slightly more than the ~$10 used, which moves the ladder by under a point. At $921.20 the price-only upside is ~1.5% and total return ~3.5%, below the 4.59% 1-yr Treasury with the 10-yr at 5.24% and rising, so there is no edge that justifies more than low conviction. I keep the mean ladder with a ~0.5-point trim (P(>=921) 0.516), fair value $935, thesis break $750, and a max weight of 10% entered in tranches around the Oct 28 FOMC and the Dec 10 Q1 print.
key_drivers: Multiple, not EPS, decides the outcome. ~40.3x forward today vs a 38x TTM median (~34-35x forward). Each forward turn on ~$25 FY28 EPS is ~$25/share, with the 10-yr at 5.24% and rising against a ~2.5% forward earnings yield.
EPS path is agreed: FY26 $20.76 ($20.61 core), FY27 ~$22.7, FY28 ~$25.0 (range $23.73-26.92). Renewal 92.3%/89.8%, both +10bp QoQ; paid members +3.8%, still decelerating.

Special dividend: 5 specials 2012-2023 with 26-43 month gaps. 33 months have passed and net cash is ~$15.1B, so ~60-65% odds of a $15-25 special going ex before Sep 2027. That is a ~$12 price-only drag, but cash in hand for a holder.
Near-term events: Sept sales Oct 7, FOMC Oct 28, Q1 FY27 Dec 10 (a special-dividend decision is historically possible in Nov-Jan).
Edge: price-only ~+1.5% to ~$935; total return ~+3.5% vs a 4.59% 1-yr Treasury. No excess-return edge at spot.
